data.narrative:
Sanctuary AI, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $130M to date, sits within a competitive frontier-tech cohort spanning 9 private peers and 1 public comparable. The peer set—including stage-adjacent companies like Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Bedrock Robotics (Series B, $1.8B), and Dexterity (Series B, $1.6B)—establishes a valuation anchor in a maturing sector.

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement to the $130M capital base, implying $221M. Peer-median analysis across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies yields a $1.6B median valuation, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer methodology carries greater weight given Sanctuary's demonstrated operational maturity relative to its funding stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $188M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $936M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around technology differentiation, customer traction, and capital efficiency relative to the peer cohort. Stage-progression alone undershoots peer valuations meaningfully, suggesting either that Sanctuary commands a discount to peer multiples or that peer valuations embed significant future-revenue expectations. Resolution of this gap hinges on revenue trajectory, gross margins, and market adoption velocity—data not present in this analysis.
